questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The trailer service air line is also called the control line or signal line.

questions.question: What happens if you stay in neutral too long when shifting gears?

options.text: You may have trouble getting into the next gear.
The vehicle will be hard to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble getting into the next gear.
questions.explanation: Staying in neutral too long when shifting can make it hard to put the vehicle into the next gear.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel drowsy while driving?

options.text: Keep driving and finish your trip.

questions.explanation: The only real solution to drowsiness while driving is to stop and sleep. Caffeine and other stimulants may help you stay awake for a short time, but they will not keep you truly alert. You will feel even more tired when the stimulants wear off.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Is a major cause of fatal crashes.
Is a good way to reach your destination quickly.
Is okay only on dry roads.
Is acceptable when traffic is light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a major cause of fatal crashes.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of fatal crashes. Never drive faster than the posted speed limit. Adjust your speed to match road conditions.

questions.question: How do you test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Remove the parking brake control knob.
Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
Release air by pressing the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, let the air supply charge fully, turn off the engine, then press the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to its emergency position when air pressure drops too low.

questions.question: When transporting hazardous materials, placards:

options.text: Must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.
Are only required for Class A licensed drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards must be displayed on all four sides of any vehicle carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: Front tire tread depth in the major grooves must be at least:
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every major groove. Other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: Loose belts in the engine compartment will:

options.text: Not turn the water pump or fan properly, causing the engine to overheat.
Make the engine run more efficiently.
Make the fan run too much, causing the engine to cool too much.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not turn the water pump or fan properly, causing the engine to overheat.
questions.explanation: Check the tightness of all belts in your engine compartment. Loose belts will not turn the water pump or fan properly, which can cause the engine to overheat.

questions.question: Parking brakes should be:

options.text: Tested only after driving for a distance.

questions.explanation: Test your parking brakes before every drive as part of your pre-trip inspection. If the parking brakes do not hold, repair the vehicle before driving.

questions.question: ____ identical placards must be placed on a vehicle carrying hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Use the posted signals to know when a train is coming.
Watch what other drivers do to know when a train is coming.
Do not depend only on signals to know when a train is coming.
Look for moving plants or bushes caused by a passing train's breeze.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not depend only on signals to know when a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Always assume a train may be coming at a railroad crossing. Do not rely only on signals or sound to tell you a train is approaching.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter a truck's cab because of:

options.text: Using the wrong type of fuel.
Not enough oil in the engine.
Tires that are not filled enough.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: If a hazardous material package is too small for its label, how should it be labeled?

options.text: Tie it with other hazardous materials and put a paper label on the outside of the bundle.
Attach the label to a tag that is firmly attached to the package.
Mark the item with a large orange dot.
Place the item in a box that has a warning label.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attach the label to a tag that is firmly attached to the package.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials must have diamond-shaped warning labels on the package. If the label does not fit, attach it to a tag that is firmly secured to the package.

questions.question: Starting in what year did new trailers have to have ABS?
questions.explanation: All trailers made after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: When a vehicle with bright headlights approaches you at night, how can you avoid being blinded?

options.text: Look toward the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights at night, look toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?

options.text: The trailer swings to the side.
The cab swings but the trailer stays straight.
The tires will likely go flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer swings to the side.
questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer may swing out and hit other vehicles. This is especially likely with lightly loaded trailers.

questions.question: Vehicle inspections are required:
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require commercial vehicle drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip.

questions.question: Tank vehicles usually have:
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles have high centers of gravity and need special care. Drivers should watch their speed when turning and driving on curves.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?

options.text: Three-quarters of a second to one second

questions.correctAnswerText: Three-quarters of a second to one second
questions.explanation: The average driver's reaction time is three-quarters of a second to one second.

questions.question: Before driving, how do you check that air reaches all trailers?

options.text: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
Close the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
Disconnect air supply lines and listen for air escaping.
Roll each trailer down a hill and test the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that air in the brake system reaches all trailers. Wait for air pressure to build, then send air to the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, the air is reaching the entire vehicle.
